Requisites
Tags: courses
Short Description: Courses or other requirements that must be completed before or at the time of enrollment in a course. Requisites may include prerequisites and corequisites.
Requisites
Requisites are courses, conditions, or other requirements that determine whether a student is eligible to enroll in a course. Requisites may be required before enrollment, at the time of enrollment, or may establish other conditions for registration.
Common types of requisites include:
Prerequisites: Courses or requirements that must be completed before enrolling in the course.
Corequisites: Courses or requirements that must be completed concurrently with the course.
Other enrollment requirements: Additional conditions that may apply to enrollment, such as minimum class standing, program or major restrictions, or other eligibility requirements.
When entering requisites in Kuali, ensure that the requirements accurately reflect the conditions under which students should be permitted to enroll.

New Temporary & Permanent Course Email
The New Temporary & Permanent Course Email is distributed to all faculty, deans, and associate and assistant deans on the last weekday of each month. Recipients then have seven days to submit comments to the CASC Chair, GEC Chair, or Dean of the Graduate School regarding any potential or perceived content overlap involving a new temporary or permanent course.
The email serves two purposes:
Provides notice of upcoming Faculty Senate review. Courses included in the email have already been reviewed and approved by their respective College Curriculum Committees and will next be reviewed by the appropriate Faculty Senate Curriculum Committee: CASC, GEC, or Graduate Council.
Provides an opportunity to identify potential content overlap. College Curriculum Committees may review the courses included in the email to identify any potential or perceived overlap with courses offered or proposed by other colleges. Any concerns can then be raised before the courses proceed to Faculty Senate Curriculum Committee review.

Short Description: Undergraduate students must complete at least 3 credits addressing each of the 12 General Education Student Learning Outcomes, organized across four areas: Knowledge, Competencies, Responsibilities, and Integrate & Apply.
General Education Outcomes

The General Education program will assess student exposure to twelve Student Learning Outcomes in four areas:
A. Build knowledge of diverse peoples and cultures and of the natural and physical world.
(A1) STEM Disciplines (A2) Social & Behavioral Sciences (A3) Humanities (A4) Art & Design
B. Develop intellectual and interdisciplinary competencies for academic and lifelong learning.
(B1) Write Effectively (B2) Communicate Effectively (B3) Mathematical, Statistical, or Computational Strategies (B4) Information Literacy
C. Exercise individual and social responsibilities.
(C1) Civic Knowledge & Responsibilies (C2) Global Responsibility (C3) Diversity & Inclusion
D. Integrate and apply these abilities and capacities, adapting them to new settings, questions, and responsibilities to lay the foundation for lifelong learning.
(D1) Integrate & Apply

General Education courses may assess one or two Student Learning Outcomes in the following configurations:
Knowledge (A) and Competency (B)
Knowledge (A) and Responsibility (C)
Competency (B) and Competency (B)
Competency (B) and Responsibility (C)
Integration (D) and Competency (B)
Integration (D) and Responsibility (C)

Kuali Basics

From your browser, navigate to Kuali Curriculum Management (CM).
Select Curriculum to open your Dashboard .
Related toolkit entry: Dashboard
From the left-hand navigation menu, select Specializations.
On the Programs page, select + New Specialization in the upper-right corner.
The following sections of this walkthrough are grouped by section of the proposal form.

Complete the following fields with your contact information.
Proposer Name Your name is automatically populated based on your Kuali account.
Proposer Title Enter your university role.
Proposer Email Enter your URI email address. This is the email reviewers will use if they have questions about your proposal.
Additional Proposer(s) Use this section to identify additional individuals who can speak to the proposed program. Individuals listed here will not receive Kuali notifications or have access to edit the proposal. Their inclusion simply provides transparency to the reviewing committees about who else is involved in or can speak to the proposal.
Inherit From Begin typing the name of the parent program, then select the program from the list.

Effective Term & Year Select the term and year in which you intend the specialization to become effective. If the selected effective term has passed the applicable deadline by the time the proposal reaches the Faculty Senate, it will automatically be updated to the next available term.
First Graduation Term Select the term and year in which you anticipate the first students will graduate with this credential.
Level Select the level of the specialization: Undergraduate, Graduate, or Dual Dual applies to ABMs and 4+1 specializations.
🔽 The following field will appear only if Dual is chosen for Level.
Dual Type Refer to the linked pages above to understand the difference between ABMs & 4+1s
Academic Calendar Select the academic calendar for the specialization: Accelerated 7-week through URI Online, or Traditional 14-week with Summer and J-Term Sessions (must coincide with parent program).
College Select the college in which the program is housed.
Department Select the department in which the program is housed.

Is this interdisciplinary? The intent of this question is to identify whether the parent program of this specialization is jointly owned by multiple academic departments. If yes, the percentage of ownership assigned to each department must be provided in the curriculum worksheet.
🔽 The following field will appear only if “Yes” is chosen for Is this interdisciplinary?
Additional Department(s) and College(s) Enter departments sharing ownership of this program.
Academic Specialization Title Enter the title of the specialization. See the linked page for title formatting guidelines.
Specialization Description List the requirements of the specialization. Only specialization-specific requirements should be listed here, and no program requirements should be duplicated.
Admission Requirements If the specialization has specific admission requirements, list them here. Otherwise, enter: “See admission requirements for {Program Title}.”
Total specialization credits (excluding program credits) Enter the number of credits required for this specialization.
🔽 The following field will appear only if ABM is chosen for Dual Type

Total double-counted course credits Enter the number of credits double counted towards this ABM.
Attach Curriculum Worksheet
Upload a curriculum worksheet outlining the courses, credits, and other requirements that make up the proposed specialization’s curriculum within its parent program. You may use the University’s standard curriculum worksheets, or you may clearly include all requirements in a word document or PDF.

🔽 This section will only appear if the Dual Type is ABM.

List all bachelor’s degrees and majors eligible for application to this ABM program. Include any specializations (sub-plans or tracks).

Topics Course
Tags: courses
Short Description: A course that allows different topics to be offered under the same course number.
Topics Course
Topics courses allow different topics to be offered under the same course number.
8.81.20 Open-ended Course. An Open-ended Course shall be administered by the department which originated it. Initially, an open-ended course shall be proposed and approved in the same manner as other permanent courses (8.81.10). Prior to offering a specific topic the content of the course shall be approved in a department meeting.
8.81.21 After approval of each offering of an open-ended course topic, a copy of the title, subtitle, and description shall be forwarded for schedule authorization to the Office of Enrollment Services via the dean of the college in which the department resides. The dean’s authorization shall ensure that no overlap exists between specific topics and existing courses.

8.81.22 A specific topic within an open-ended course may be offered three times. After three offerings the topic shall be approved through the appropriate channels as either a permanent course or as a permanent topic within an open-ended course and shall be included in the University Catalog.
